q.t: Two or more substances mixed together form a…
q.e: Separation methods use differences between components.

q.t: Removing small stones from rice by hand is…
q.e: Works when the unwanted bits are few.

q.t: Beating stalks to separate grain is…
q.e: Traditionally against a wooden log.

q.t: Using wind to blow husk away from grain is…
q.e: Light husk flies; heavy grain falls.

q.t: Separating bran from flour with a mesh is…
q.e: Fine particles pass; bigger ones stay.

q.t: Settling of heavy insoluble solid at the bottom is…
q.e: Like tea leaves settling in a pot.

q.t: Pouring off liquid leaving the settled solid is…
q.e: Tilt gently and pour.

q.t: What stays on the filter paper is the…
q.e: The liquid that passes through is the filtrate.

q.t: Salt is obtained from seawater by…
q.e: Water evaporates in shallow pits, leaving salt.

q.t: A soop is a…
q.e: Grain is dropped from it into the wind.

q.t: Winnowing separates on the basis of…
q.e: Light parts blow away.

q.t: Sieving separates on the basis of…
q.e: Small particles pass through holes.

q.t: Why doesn't winnowing work in a closed room?
o: There's no moving air to carry husk away
q.e: Winnowing needs moving air.

q.t: Why is handpicking a bad method for a lot of husk?
o: It only works when unwanted bits are few
q.e: It would take forever.

q.t: Why doesn't decantation separate completely?
o: Some solid still comes with the poured liquid
q.e: For a clean separation, filter.

q.t: Why does cloth work as a filter?
o: There are small pores between its threads
q.e: Particles larger than the pores are stopped.

q.t: Why can't a filter catch salt dissolved in water?
o: Dissolved salt has broken up completely in the water
q.e: Use evaporation for dissolved solids.

q.t: White patches on dark clothes after sweating are…
q.e: Same as getting salt from seawater.

q.t: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is a source of…
q.e: Salt is obtained there by evaporation.

q.t: Modern threshers do…
q.e: Both steps at once.

q.t: Which method for separating sand from water completely?
q.e: Sand is insoluble; a filter catches it.

q.t: Which method to get sugar back from sugar solution?
q.e: Sugar is dissolved; evaporate the water.

q.t: Oil and water can be separated by…
q.e: Oil forms a separate layer and can be poured off.

q.t: Pebbles and sand at a construction site are separated by…
q.e: Solid–solid mixture of different sizes.

q.t: For sieving to work, the hole size must be…
o: Between the sizes of the two particles
q.e: Otherwise nothing gets separated.

q.t: A tea strainer stops tea leaves but not mud. Why?
o: Mud particles are smaller than its holes
q.e: Filter choice depends on particle size.

q.t: Muddy water needs a filter that is…
o: Finer, like cloth or filter paper
q.e: Smaller pores catch finer particles.

q.t: Washing rice and pouring off the water uses…
q.e: Rice settles; water is poured off.

q.t: Why does Ayurveda dry medicinal plants in shade?
o: To evaporate excess water but keep the medicine
q.e: An everyday use of evaporation.

q.t: Roasted peanuts rubbed and blown — the skins fly off. This is…
q.e: Light skins blown away by moving air.

q.t: A mixture of sand, salt and water. Order of methods to get dry salt:
o: Filter out sand, then evaporate the water
q.e: Filtration removes insoluble sand; evaporation recovers dissolved salt.

q.t: A mixture of iron filings and sand could be separated by…
q.e: Iron is magnetic; sand isn't — a difference to exploit.

q.t: Every separation method works by exploiting…
q.e: Size, weight, solubility, magnetism…

q.t: Black peppers removed from pulao by hand. Why handpicking?
o: They're few, and differ in colour and size
q.e: Handpicking suits a few easily seen items.

q.t: Charcoal, sand and cotton can all act as…
q.e: Different filter materials for different particle sizes.

q.t: Seawater is kept in shallow pits rather than deep tanks because…
q.e: Large exposed surface evaporates faster.

q.t: Chalk powder in water: decantation or filtration for a clean result?
q.e: Decantation leaves some solid; filtration separates completely.

q.t: The liquid that passes through a filter is called…
q.e: Residue stays on the filter.

q.t: Boiling a salt solution in a china dish leaves…
q.e: Water boils away; salt remains.

q.t: Which separation uses BOTH a difference in weight and moving air?
q.e: Heavy grain falls; light husk is carried by wind.
